To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mid term outcome of patients with native aorta coarctation treated with percutaneous treatment was strongly related to the initial residual gradient and that when the residual gradient was ≤ 10 mmHg, patients had similar mid term results whether they were treated with balloon angioplasties alone or with stent implantation.
In adult patients with native coaractation of the aortas, mid-term results are strongly related to the residual gradient.

the mid term outcome of adult patients with native coarction of the aorta receiving percutaneous dilatation is strongly related to immediate residual gradient, and that when treating these cases, effort should be made to achieve gradients under 10mm Hg, either with angioplasty or stent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the treatment of adults with native aortic arch coarctation by means of percutaneous techniques.
the use of balloon angioplasty with and without stents in native coarctations in adults.
the use of stents to treat adult patients with aortic coarction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stent implantation in native adult coarctation is not a routine procedure, but it may be indicated in selected patients.
the best results are obtained when a stent is used for patients with hypoplasia of the isthmus or a tubular coarction.
the type of coarctation (discrete, hypoplastic isthmic, tubular) is the most important risk factor, and the residual gradient is the most important predictor of outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immediate residual gradient after percutaneous dilatation is the only predictor of mid term outcome and that the implantation of stent should be considered when the residual gradient is ≥ 10 mm Hq.
stenting is the best treatment for native coarctations with hypoplastic or tubular coartation, and that balloon angioplasty is the best treatment when the coarctations are discrete.
stent implantation is a safe and effective procedure in native aortic coartation of the aortic arch in adults.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immediate residual gradient should be considered a major risk factor in the mid term outcome of patients with native aorta coarctation.
a residual gradient of <10 mm Hg after percutaneous dilatation is associated with a better mid term outcome.
the type of coarctation, the residual gradient, and the use of the stent were the main predictors of the outcome in our study population.
